sections.title: Factors That Affect Your Jeevan Labh Premium

items: Age of Policyholder: The younger you are, the lower your premium.
Sum Assured: A higher coverage amount means a higher premium.
Policy Term: Longer terms generally have slightly lower annualized premiums but are paid for more years.
Mode of Payment: Yearly payments are cheaper than monthly payments due to 'modal loading'.
Riders: Optional add-ons like Accidental Death Benefit increase the cost.
High Sum Assured Rebates: LIC offers a discount on higher sum assured amounts, which our calculator includes.

sections.title: LIC Jeevan Labh Maturity Calculator (Returns Explained)

content.text: The maturity value is the key attraction of Jeevan Labh. It is calculated as:
Maturity Value = Basic Sum Assured + Vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses + Final Additional Bonus (FAB)

Example: For a 30-year-old taking a ₹10 lakh policy for a 25-year term (16-year PPT), the total premium paid is ~₹6.75 lakh. Based on current illustrative bonus rates (~₹47 per 1000 SA), the estimated maturity could be around ₹27.50 lakh. This represents a safe, tax-free return of around 5-6% IRR, combined with life cover.

sections.title: LIC Jeevan Labh Benefits at a Glance

items: Pay for Less, Get for More: The key benefit is the limited premium payment term. For a 25-year policy, you only pay for 16 years.
Dual Advantage: It combines life insurance protection with a disciplined savings plan, ensuring a lump sum at maturity.
Tax Efficiency: Premiums paid are deductible under Section 80C, and the maturity amount is tax-free under Section 10(10D).
Liquidity Options: Loan and surrender facilities are available after two full years of premium payments.

items.q: What is the premium of LIC Jeevan Labh for 10 lakh?
items.a: For a 30-year-old taking a 25-year term, the yearly premium for a ₹10 lakh cover is approximately ₹42,200. This can be calculated instantly using our tool.

items.q: How is LIC Jeevan Labh maturity value calculated?
items.a: The maturity value is the sum of the Basic Sum Assured, all vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses declared over the policy term, and a one-time Final Additional Bonus (FAB), if any.

items.q: What are LIC Jeevan Labh bonus rates 2025?
items.a: Bonus rates are declared by LIC annually and are not guaranteed. For recent years, the illustrative rate for Jeevan Labh has been in the range of ₹43-₹47 per ₹1,000 Sum Assured, depending on the policy term.

items.q: Which is better: LIC Jeevan Labh or Jeevan Umang?
items.a: Jeevan Labh is a limited-pay endowment plan with a fixed maturity date, ideal for goal-based savings. Jeevan Umang is a whole-life plan that provides annual survival benefits after the PPT and matures at age 100. Umang has higher premiums but offers lifelong cover and income.

items.q: Can I take a loan on my LIC Jeevan Labh policy?
items.a: Yes, a loan can be availed on the policy after at least two full years' premiums have been paid, subject to terms and conditions.

items.q: Is LIC Jeevan Labh a good investment?
items.a: Jeevan Labh is a safe, traditional insurance-cum-savings product offering tax-free returns of around 5-6% IRR. It's suitable for risk-averse individuals seeking disciplined savings and life cover, but not for those seeking high, market-linked growth.

items.q: How much is the LIC Jeevan Labh 1 crore premium?
items.a: For a 30-year-old with a 25-year term, the yearly premium for a ₹1 crore sum assured is approximately ₹4,15,000. Use our calculator to get an exact figure for your age.

items.q: What is the surrender value in Jeevan Labh?
items.a: The policy acquires a surrender value after two full years of premium payment. The Guaranteed Surrender Value is a percentage of total premiums paid, but the Special Surrender Value, which depends on LIC's discretion and bonus rates, is usually higher.
